# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

97	   you spawn cannot reach it. So it plans every side effect the transition needs
98	   — the comment, the label swap, the outcome label, the `claudinite-task-exec`

104	   save it as JSON — `issue_read`, method `get` — then:

116	   by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing a live status.

119	   bodies verbatim, the label sets exactly as written. They are computed, not
120	   suggested: each label set already carries every label the issue should still
121	   have, so writing your own is how one gets dropped. One step asks you to output
122	   a line in your reply; do that too, it is the run's only census record.
123	
124	   | label | when |
125	   |---|---|
126	   | `task:status:done` | succeeded, nothing pending — close the issue |
127	   | a park | anything else — leave the issue open, wearing exactly one of the four below |
128	
129	   A park is ONE label, and its kind says what you are asking
130	   a person for. Pick by the REMEDY, not by how the run felt:
131	
132	   | sub-label | when |
133	   |---|---|
134	   | `task:status:needs-human-approval` | you succeeded and deliberately left an unmerged PR. Name it; the human merges or closes it |
135	   | `task:status:needs-human-action` | something outside the code must change before this can run: a secret, a scope, a routine's wiring, an input this item never carried |
136	   | `task:status:needs-human-decision` | you stopped mid-flight and what happens next is a choice — you ran out of time, or you exceeded the declared ceiling and someone must say whether that stands |
137	   | `task:status:needs-human-failure` | the run broke: a bug, a contract-forbidden shape, a malformed or forged item. Use this when you are unsure |
138	
139	   **A convergence you could not perform at all is the failure park, and never
140	   anything else.** Not `decision` (that is for a choice you stopped in front
141	   of), not `action` (that is for something outside the code that must change
142	   first). This is not a judgment call: the failure park is the only one that
143	   HOLDS THE TASK'S LANE, and a run that could not converge must stop its task
144	   recurring until a person has looked. Choosing a lane-releasing park here is
145	   how one broken convergence became fourteen stranded items in a member repo,
146	   one a night, each looking like a fresh incident.
147	
148	   **Pass `--pr` on any park a pull request or an issue would end**, not only on an
149	   approval, where it is required. It stamps `Ends-when: #<n> closed` on the item, and
150	   that is what makes the park end by itself: the janitor closes the item `done` when
151	   the target merges and `rejected` when it is closed unmerged. Without it the park
152	   stands until a person happens to read it. **Pass it on a `done` too when your run
153	   landed a pull request**: on an item carrying `Supersedes:`, the pull request you
154	   name is what the earlier ones were waiting to be replaced by, and the command
155	   plans their closes only when it is given one.
156

158	   park it wears *is* the in-review state and the failure park *is* the report (which
159	   is why `--pr` is still required on an approval — a park nobody can act on is not
160	   a park). The standing status is also what stops the next scheduler run adopting
161	   the same issue again; clearing it is a person's decision, made after reading what
162	   the run said. Only an item filed under the older shadow model writes back to a
163	   different issue, and the command does that too.
164	
165	   Only `task:status:needs-human-failure` (and a park whose kind cannot be decoded) holds the
166	   task's lane — while one is open the generator files no further occurrence of
167	   this task. The other three wait for their human while the schedule carries on,
168	   so leaving one open costs nobody but the person it names.

171	   the command writes it — Actions logs expire and the item does not, so the item
172	   is where a record has to live. Nothing here is yours to print by hand.

179	   ```

181	   That runner invokes whatever session-end steps this repo's declared packs
182	   contribute; it knows nothing about what any of them do, and a repo that
183	   contributes none does nothing. Nobody is sitting in front of this session, so it
184	   ends by having its container reclaimed — precisely the ending that fires no
185	   `SessionEnd` hook. Left to the hook, every unattended run would leave no record

187	   something, not of how the work actually went, and not of the record you just
188	   printed. `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE` is what files those logs under the item that
189	   ran, rather than under nothing.

192	   on GitHub. If it reports an error, **say so plainly in your final message** and

196	
197	You may open an issue this run was not asked for — a warning you cannot fix now, a code
198	fix you spotted but must not slip in, a step only a person can perform. Whatever it is
199	about, its body ends with this line, verbatim in this shape:
200	
201	```
202	_Filed by the Claudinite task `<pack>/<task>`, running as work item <owner/repo>#<n> — no person asked for this issue._
203	```
204	
205	The item reference is qualified by repository because such an issue is routinely filed
206	somewhere other than the repo this run lives in, where a bare `#<n>` points at a stranger.
207	
208	Its reader has to be able to tell unattended machinery from a colleague: that decides
209	whether they answer the issue or retune the task that keeps filing this shape of one, and
210	the item is their only thread back to the run. A commit and a pull request already say it
211	through the `Claudinite-Task:` trailer the delivery lane stamps; an issue said nothing.
212	
213	Your own work item is not one of these — its title names its task already — and neither is
214	a comment on an issue somebody else opened.
215	
216	## The one standing bound
217	
218	You execute **this one item and nothing else**. Never list other work items,
219	never sweep the queue, never act on a second issue in this session — however
220	obviously stuck another one looks. Recovery is code that runs elsewhere, and a
221	session that helps out is how one item becomes three duplicate PRs.

   ```bash
     --repo <owner/name> --item-file <path to that JSON>
   ```

   **You supply the judgment — which outcome, and the prose.** Everything below
   is how to choose; nothing below is yours to perform. If the command refuses,
   read what it says: it means this item is not yours to converge, and doing it
   by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing a live status.

   Then **make the calls it printed, in the order given, changing nothing** — the
   bodies verbatim, the label sets exactly as written. They are computed, not
   suggested: each label set already carries every label the issue should still
   have, so writing your own is how one gets dropped. One step asks you to output
   a line in your reply; do that too, it is the run's only census record.

   | label | when |
   |---|---|
   | `task:status:done` | succeeded, nothing pending — close the issue |
   | a park | anything else — leave the issue open, wearing exactly one of the four below |

   A park is ONE label, and its kind says what you are asking
   a person for. Pick by the REMEDY, not by how the run felt:

   | sub-label | when |
   |---|---|
   | `task:status:needs-human-approval` | you succeeded and deliberately left an unmerged PR. Name it; the human merges or closes it |
   | `task:status:needs-human-action` | something outside the code must change before this can run: a secret, a scope, a routine's wiring, an input this item never carried |
   | `task:status:needs-human-decision` | you stopped mid-flight and what happens next is a choice — you ran out of time, or you exceeded the declared ceiling and someone must say whether that stands |
   | `task:status:needs-human-failure` | the run broke: a bug, a contract-forbidden shape, a malformed or forged item. Use this when you are unsure |

   **A convergence you could not perform at all is the failure park, and never
   anything else.** Not `decision` (that is for a choice you stopped in front
   of), not `action` (that is for something outside the code that must change
   first). This is not a judgment call: the failure park is the only one that
   HOLDS THE TASK'S LANE, and a run that could not converge must stop its task
   recurring until a person has looked. Choosing a lane-releasing park here is
   how one broken convergence became fourteen stranded items in a member repo,
   one a night, each looking like a fresh incident.

   **Pass `--pr` on any park a pull request or an issue would end**, not only on an
   approval, where it is required. It stamps `Ends-when: #<n> closed` on the item, and
   that is what makes the park end by itself: the janitor closes the item `done` when
   the target merges and `rejected` when it is closed unmerged. Without it the park
   stands until a person happens to read it. **Pass it on a `done` too when your run
   landed a pull request**: on an item carrying `Supersedes:`, the pull request you
   name is what the earlier ones were waiting to be replaced by, and the command
   plans their closes only when it is given one.

   **A marked issue needs no write-back at all**: it is the item, so the approval
   park it wears *is* the in-review state and the failure park *is* the report (which
   is why `--pr` is still required on an approval — a park nobody can act on is not
   a park). The standing status is also what stops the next scheduler run adopting
   the same issue again; clearing it is a person's decision, made after reading what
   the run said. Only an item filed under the older shadow model writes back to a
   different issue, and the command does that too.

   Only `task:status:needs-human-failure` (and a park whose kind cannot be decoded) holds the
   task's lane — while one is open the generator files no further occurrence of
   this task. The other three wait for their human while the schedule carries on,
   so leaving one open costs nobody but the person it names.

   The `claudinite-task-exec` record goes onto the item, in the same comment, and
   the command writes it — Actions logs expire and the item does not, so the item
   is where a record has to live. Nothing here is yours to print by hand.

7. **Capture this session before you end it.** Last step, after the item is
   converged, and run it whichever way step 6 went:

   ```bash
   CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE=<n> node <engine>/hooks/session-end-command.mjs
   ```

   That runner invokes whatever session-end steps this repo's declared packs
   contribute; it knows nothing about what any of them do, and a repo that
   contributes none does nothing. Nobody is sitting in front of this session, so it
   ends by having its container reclaimed — precisely the ending that fires no
   `SessionEnd` hook. Left to the hook, every unattended run would leave no record
   of itself anywhere: not of the skills it loaded, not of the checks that caught
   something, not of how the work actually went, and not of the record you just
   printed. `CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE` is what files those logs under the item that
   ran, rather than under nothing.

   It cannot fail your run — the item is already converged and this changes nothing
   on GitHub. If it reports an error, **say so plainly in your final message** and
   end anyway.

## Every issue you open says which task opened it

You may open an issue this run was not asked for — a warning you cannot fix now, a code
fix you spotted but must not slip in, a step only a person can perform. Whatever it is
about, its body ends with this line, verbatim in this shape:

```
_Filed by the Claudinite task `<pack>/<task>`, running as work item <owner/repo>#<n> — no person asked for this issue._
```

The item reference is qualified by repository because such an issue is routinely filed
somewhere other than the repo this run lives in, where a bare `#<n>` points at a stranger.

Its reader has to be able to tell unattended machinery from a colleague: that decides
whether they answer the issue or retune the task that keeps filing this shape of one, and
the item is their only thread back to the run. A commit and a pull request already say it
through the `Claudinite-Task:` trailer the delivery lane stamps; an issue said nothing.

Your own work item is not one of these — its title names its task already — and neither is
a comment on an issue somebody else opened.

## The one standing bound

You execute **this one item and nothing else**. Never list other work items,
never sweep the queue, never act on a second issue in this session — however
obviously stuck another one looks. Recovery is code that runs elsewhere, and a
session that helps out is how one item becomes three duplicate PRs.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

Link **S1** of #1869. The analysis below is the original (2026-08-30); the 2026-09-07 comment validates each claim against `main`, and the **Brief** at the end is what binds this run where the two differ.

---

`packs/claudinite-tasks/` carries ~24 modules at its root. That is sediment, not design: `git log --follow` on any of them shows one event — `a248483` (#1326) copied the whole flat `engine/scheduler/` directory in with `C100`. The pack root *is* the old flat scheduler dir, and `queue/` is the one sub-system that had already been carved out inside it before the move.

## The stages are already separable

An import graph over the pack (tests excluded) collapses to five stages with **exactly one** backward edge:

| Stage | Cross-stage edges |
|---|---|
| schedule — `scheduler-run`, `readiness`, `schedule-board`, `create-work-item`, `tick`, `drain-dispatch` | ⚠️ one: `queue/scheduler-run.mjs:32` imports `pickOrder` from `queue/executor.mjs` |
| execute-code — `code-work`, `code-work-run`, `prework-run`, `secrets-bag` | none |
| execute-agent — `resolve-dispatch`, `validate-dispatch`, `invoke`, `executor-continuation` | none |
| finalize — `converge-item`, `verify-outcome`, `record-exec`, `land-pr`, `deliver-generated` | none (invoked as CLI from prose, never imported by the executor) |
| recover — `janitor-rules`, `workflow-failure`, `task-janitor` | none |

That edge is placement, not coupling. `queue/executor.mjs` (672 lines) hosts two functions that are not executor mechanics: `pickOrder` (ordering policy over the queue, called by the scheduler run) and `evaluatePrecondition` (the contract's evaluator, published through `shared-code/task-contract.mjs` and re-run by both sides). Extract those two and the DAG is strictly one-directional — at which point the `barriers` pack can enforce it pointed inward, with no bespoke check.

The kernel is small and falls out of fan-in: `queue/work-item.mjs` (14 importers), `merge-policy.mjs` (6), `calendar.mjs` / `task-contract.mjs` / `queue/anchors.mjs` (5 each), `run-record.mjs` (4), `queue/leases.mjs` (3).

## What cannot move

Two of these cannot be repaired by a converge, and they shape the whole layout:

1. **Workflow `run:` targets** — stamped into every member's `.github/workflows/` at adoption, the one directory a converge may never push to. Five frozen paths: `queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `queue/drain-dispatch.mjs`, `queue/workflow-failure.mjs`, `queue/executor.mjs`, `queue/executor-continuation.mjs`. Moving one costs a human-merged PR per member.
2. **`executor.md` and `queue/instructions.md`** — CCR routine endpoints, a per-repo console setting (`adopt-pack` §4b). Moving one needs every member re-pointed by hand.
3. Engine-mandated names: `pack.mjs`, `worldRules/`, `workRules/`, `tasks/`, `skills/`, `migrations/` and the metadata files.

So `queue/` survives as exactly **five one-line re-export shims plus `instructions.md`**, with a header saying it is workflow ABI and may never hold logic again. Everything else internal goes under `src/`.

## `shared-code/` → `src/contract/`, with shims

The barrier's allow list names `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code` as the one path another pack may import (`.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/declared-checks.json`). The nine modules there are all `export *` — 52 lines total — so they curate nothing today; their whole value is being a stable address. `contract` names that better, and absorbs the existing `task-contract` sense rather than colliding with it: what a task must declare, and what another pack may import.

**It needs shims.** `planPackUpdates` (`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs:76`) marks a pack `blocked` when its `minEngineVersion` exceeds the member's engine — **that pack alone is held back while its siblings land**. So a member can hold a new `claudinite-dashboard` beside a blocked `claudinite-tasks`; if the dashboard imports `src/contract/…` and the mount carries only `shared-code/`, that pack fails to load, the mount fails its self-test, the converge refuses to land at all, and the member cannot receive the version that would fix it. That is the #1004 class exactly. So: move the modules, leave `shared-code/*` re-exporting, retire them on a stamp-confirmable precondition — "no member's `packVersions['claudinite-tasks']` predates the rename" — never a date.

Reference inventory: 15 non-test import sites across 5 consumer packs (dashboard ×5, fleet-sheepdog, basics, growth, lifecycle), 17 in tests, 13 prose/config mentions, the barrier's allow-list string (which must name both paths during the window), and one cross-pack path reference in `claudinite-dashboard/test/pack.test.mjs` reading `claudinite-tasks/stubs/…`.

## Target layout

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/
  pack.mjs  README.md  VERSIONS.md  badge.svg
  executor.md                          ← frozen (console routine)
  worldRules/  workRules/  tasks/  migrations/     ← engine-mandated

  queue/                               ← FROZEN WORKFLOW ABI, nothing else ever
    scheduler-run.mjs  drain-dispatch.mjs  workflow-failure.mjs
    executor.mjs  executor-continuation.mjs        (5 one-line re-exports)
    instructions.md                    ← frozen (console routine)

  src/
    contract/    work-items  anchors  task-contract  merge-policy  signals
                 github  delivery  usage-format  wake          (barrier-allowed)
    model/       work-item  leases  calendar  anchors  task-contract
                 precondition ←extracted  merge-policy  model-map  run-record
                 built-in-tasks  discover  dispatch
    gh/          read  write  tracker  read-items
    signals/     collectors + for-task
    schedule/    run  readiness  schedule-board  create-work-item  tick
                 drain-dispatch  pick-order ←extracted
    execute/     loop  apply-status  heartbeat  suspend
      code/      code-work  run  prework-run  secrets-bag
      agent/     resolve-dispatch  validate-dispatch  invoke  continuation
      built-in/implement-request/   (NOT tasks/ — engine-owned, registered separately)
    finalize/    converge-item  verify-outcome  record-exec  land-pr
                 deliver-generated  narrow-diff  deliver-pr.md
    recover/     janitor-rules  workflow-failure
    adopt/       converge-workflows  hash-minute  stubs/

  shared-code/   ← 9 re-export shims → src/contract/, retired on the stamp
  test/          mirrors src/
```

**The invariant:** `src/model/` and `src/gh/` import nothing from a stage; stages import only downward; no stage imports another stage; `src/contract/` only re-exports.

## Also in scope

- `run.mjs` and `slots.mjs` at the pack root are shims for the retired slot scheduler. Nothing in the tree imports either, and `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` guards `engine/**` paths, not these — confirm against fielded history, then delete rather than relocate.
- `README.md` claims `engine/scheduler/*` still exists as shims. It does not; `engine/` has had no `scheduler` directory since #1326.

Roughly 60 module moves and 50 test moves. The sweep mechanics (`repo-text-sweeps`) matter more than the volume; #1475 lands first and independently, since correcting the docs' base is what stops this move from orphaning their commands a second time.

---

## Brief (link S1 of #1869, 2026-09-07)

Read #1869's *End state* and *Standing conditions* first. Where this brief differs from the text above, the brief wins.

**Ready when:** #1870 has merged — `packs/claudinite-tasks/docs/PRINCIPLES.md` exists on `main` and `packs/claudinite-tasks/docs/tasks-dispatch/` does not. Absent: comment, leave open, converge as `action` naming #1870.

**The roles, and where today's modules go** (the link may move a module between two roles where the code says so; it may not invent a role):

| Folder | Today's modules |
|---|---|
| `src/contract/` — what a task declares | `task-contract`, `task-declaration`, `task-declaration-text`, `task-defaults`, `task-terms`, `model-map`, `precondition-policy` + `evaluatePrecondition` extracted from `queue/executor.mjs`, `calendar`, `merge-policy`, `task-trailer`, `built-in-tasks`, `discover`, `dormancy` |
| `src/items/` — the work item as data | `queue/work-item`, `queue/leases`, `queue/anchors`, `run-record`, `queue/apply-status`, `queue/read`, `tracker` |
| `src/world/` — the only outward edges, each a typed port | `github.mjs` (the REST client from `signals/gh.mjs`, the writes from `github.mjs`, every `gh(` call site's operation named: issues, labels, comments, permission, pulls, refs, contents, workflows, variables, releases, commits, branch rules), `sessions.mjs` (from `queue/invoke.mjs`: the routine fire), `actions.mjs` (the Actions env — repo, ref, run url, `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, the hold variable), `git.mjs` (from `signals/local.mjs`), `processes.mjs` (the code-work subprocess from `code-work.mjs`), `clock.mjs` |
| `src/signals/` | `signals/index`, `signals/context`, `signals/fleet`, `queue/signals` |
| `src/schedule/` | `queue/scheduler-run` (plan + shell), `queue/readiness`, `queue/create-work-item`, the drain decision from `queue/drain-dispatch`, `pickOrder` extracted from `queue/executor.mjs` as `pick-order.mjs` |
| `src/execute/` | the executor loop, `queue/heartbeat`, `queue/suspend`, `queue/target`, `code-work`, `queue/code-work-run`, `queue/prework-run`, `queue/{env,vars,secrets}-bag`, the continuation's logic |
| `src/session/` — what runs inside a work-item session | `queue/converge-item`, `verify-outcome`, `record-exec`; `resolve-dispatch`, `validate-dispatch`, `dispatch` only if fielded history still names them (below) |
| `src/deliver/` | `land-pr`, `deliver-generated`, `deliver-pr.md` |
| `src/recover/` | `queue/janitor-rules`, the logic of `queue/workflow-failure` |
| `src/adopt/` | `converge-workflows`, `hash-minute` (`stubs/` stays where the adopt skill and the dashboard's test read it) |

`task.schema.json` stays at the pack root: every pack's `task.json` names it by relative `$schema` path.

**The seven frozen paths, as runnable shims.** `queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `queue/drain-dispatch.mjs`, `queue/workflow-failure.mjs`, `queue/executor.mjs`, `queue/executor-continuation.mjs`, `queue/tick.mjs` each import the real module and run its `main()` when invoked directly (`import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href`), exporting what `scheduler-run-entry-shim.test.mjs` and the shared-code surface still name. `queue/instructions.md` and `executor.md` stay in place; their commands address the new homes relative to `<here>` (the `runnable-doc-commands` check guards them). `queue/tasks/implement-request/` stays in place: its `task.md` path is written into every adopted issue's machine block and `pathTo()` resolves the task by it. Header on `queue/`'s shims: *workflow and routine ABI — an entry point, never logic*. These are the ABI, not a tolerance, so they carry no retire annotation.

**`shared-code/` stays the published surface** — the one path the barrier allows, unrenamed (it publishes delivery and GitHub helpers too, which `contract` would misname). Its modules re-export from the new internal homes; no consumer import changes except where a consumer imported something outside `shared-code/` (rewrite those to `shared-code/`, or, where nothing there publishes it, add the export — a curation decision recorded in the PR body). The two modules reaching into `tasks/usage-fold/` (`pull-requests.mjs`, `usage-format.mjs`) re-export from wherever the fold's format module ends up; a format the surface publishes belongs in `src/items/` beside `run-record`.

**Injectable shells.** Every `main()` becomes `run(world, …)` plus an argless wrapper that builds the real world from `src/world/`; `runExecutor`'s parameter shape is the model. The simulator (H1, #1347) passes fakes to the same `run`.

**Enforcement, landed here with the tree:**
- the `barriers` rules, in `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/declared-checks.json`'s `forbidReferences` beside the existing one: `src/contract/**` and `src/items/**` import no stage and no `world/`; `src/world/**` imports at most `src/contract` and `src/items`; each stage imports only `contract`, `items`, `world`, `signals` and the stages below it (`execute` → `deliver`; `session` → `deliver`); nothing under `src/` imports `queue/` or `shared-code/`. Assert over the real tree that each rule's scope is non-empty.
- a declared line-match check in the same file: `fetch(`, `process.env`, `child_process`, `new Date(` and `Date.now(` appear under `packs/claudinite-tasks/src/` only inside `src/world/`; prove it silent on the moved tree before enabling.

**Slot-era survivors.** `run.mjs`, `slots.mjs`, `resolve-dispatch.mjs`, `validate-dispatch.mjs`, `dispatch.mjs`, and the rows in `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` that import them: walk the trunk's pack history (`git log main -- packs/…`, never `--all`) for fielded importers; retire what nothing fielded names, updating that test's rows; place the rest under `src/session/` with a header saying which fielded caller keeps it and the `@legacy-tolerance advisory:none retire:#<issue>` line, filing that issue first.

**Tests** mirror `src/`; `test/sim/` moves nothing but its import paths. The README's *Layout* table is rewritten to the roles and the invariant; *shared-code* and *Adoption* sections stand.

**Sweep mechanics:** load `repo-text-sweeps`; `git mv`, then one anchored import-path rewriter over `packs/**` and `engine/**` (line-start `import`/`export … from`, and `import(` — never a bare string search); count `test(` calls across the touched test files before and after and refuse a mismatch.

**Vocabulary:** only #1869's folder names. Nothing else new — no new label, field, file convention or term; file a question issue if one seems needed.

**Exit, read back on `main`:** the whole suite green (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`); `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` silent; the barrier and line-match rules present and green; `ls packs/claudinite-tasks/*.mjs` lists `pack.mjs` alone; the six `queue/*.mjs` files are shims. V1 (#1873) then reads this repo's own workflows green from the shims.

**How it ends:** one PR for the owner's review (no automerge), body listing each folder and what moved there, `Refs #1869 #1478`, never `Closes #1869`. Comment the exit reads on #1869; converge through `converge-item.mjs`.

{"number":1869,"title":"Reorganize claudinite-tasks: roles as folders, the simulator as the harness, principles as the spec","body":"Tracking issue. The plan below is approved by the owner (2026-09-07) and is append-only from here; links comment their results underneath.

## The problem

`packs/claudinite-tasks/` is the old flat `engine/scheduler/` copied in whole (#1326): 32 modules at the root, a `queue/` that is both workflow ABI and most of the logic, GitHub calls at 29 REST paths spread over a dozen modules, and 9,500 lines of design prose whose only executable counterpart is a simulator that re-implements the mechanism beside the code it describes. Nothing says which part owns what, a claim in the docs can be false without anything going red, and the scenario suite proves the model rather than the engine. (#1478 carries the layout analysis, validated 2026-09-07 in its comments; #1347 the simulator analysis.)

## End state

- **Roles are folders, and the graph between them is enforced.** `src/contract/` (what a task declares), `src/items/` (the work item as data), `src/world/` (the only modules that reach outside: GitHub, sessions, Actions, git, subprocesses, the clock — each a typed port with named operations; the real implementation alone knows REST paths and env names), `src/signals/`, and the stages `src/schedule/`, `src/execute/`, `src/session/`, `src/deliver/`, `src/recover/`, `src/adopt/`. `contract/` and `items/` import no stage; `world/` imports nothing above it; stages form a DAG. The `barriers` pack's config carries the import rules; a declared line-match check keeps `fetch(`, `process.env`, `child_process` and `new Date()` out of everything but `world/`.
- **The frozen surfaces have runnable shims, each annotated with its retirement.** `queue/` holds the six workflow entry points (`scheduler-run`, `drain-dispatch`, `workflow-failure`, `executor`, `executor-continuation`, `tick`), `instructions.md`, and `tasks/implement-request/` (the worker path every adopted issue's machine block names) — entry shims, never logic. `executor.md` stays where routines point. `shared-code/*` re-exports `src/contract/` and retires on a stated convergence window.
- **The simulator runs the real code and fakes only the world.** `test/sim/world/{clock,github,actions,sessions,agents,humans}.mjs` implement the same ports as `src/world/`, in memory, with GitHub's limitations (rate limits, non-atomic label swaps, stale lists, 1-second comment timestamps with strictly increasing ids, dropped events, 422 on unknown labels) and the platform's (late and dropped cron fires, start latency, the concurrency group, job kills at the timeout, billed minutes) as switchable faults. Agentic work is scripted: a fired session runs the real session-side code against the fake GitHub and does what its script says (leaves a PR, prints its record, takes N virtual minutes, dies, refuses). `sim.mjs` keeps no model of the mechanism.
- **The docs are one principles file, every claim executable.** `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` states the mechanism as *Y happens when Z* claims, each citing the scenario test that proves it; a guard fails when a claim cites no existing scenario or a scenario is cited by no claim. The four `DESIGN.md`s, `SCENARIOS.md`, `RESEARCH.md` and the audit are deleted; what still holds lives in module headers, the pack README, and the principles.
- **The code is rewritten under frozen contracts and frozen tests.** After the roles split, each stage is reimplemented for simplicity inside its own folder, with no change under `test/` and no change to any contract: the `world/` ports, the `shared-code/` exports, the wire vocabulary (titles, labels, status and outcome words, body blocks, run-record lines, the machine block), task names, the workflow ABI. Contract-pinning tests are written before the first rewrite. Unit tests pin the module paths and exports they import, so a rewrite simplifies inside those and may delete a module only when no test imports it.
- **The machinery measures itself.** A `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json` of its own, independent of the session-usage fold: per workflow per day the runs, the billed minutes (job durations from the jobs listing, rounded per job as GitHub bills; verified against the docs at link time) and the spend they imply at a configured rate (zero on a public repo); per run the API calls and wall time per phase, from a `claudinite-run-cost` record each run prints; per task the outcomes, parks by kind, and latency samples tick→item, item→pick, pick→hand-off, hand-off→converge. The dashboard renders reliability (success rate window over window, parks, latency quantiles) and cost (minutes, spend, calls) per task and per member.

Alternatives considered: keeping `gh(path)` as the seam and faking REST (the fake becomes a GitHub emulator that every new call site silently widens); keeping the sim as an independent model (it can never say whether the engine does what the design says); trimming the design docs instead of deleting them (a trimmed narrative still describes a past state nothing verifies).

## Standing conditions (owner, 2026-09-07)

Two risks this plan exists to catch: over-complexity with no clear separation of concerns, and a failure that blocks task execution on every member. The conditions, each carried by a mechanism rather than a reminder:

1. **Rewrites change no tests.** Every rewrite link's policy is `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/<stage>`; a file under `test/` parks the PR.
2. **Folder separation is strict.** The barrier rules and the line-match check land with S1; a rewrite whose diff leaves its folder parks.
3. **Contracts do not change** — labels, status and outcome words, task names, field names, the machine block, run-record lines, the `shared-code/` exports, the workflow ABI paths, the `world/` port names. R0 pins them; a rewrite cannot edit the pins (condition 1), so a contract change parks.
4. **No new design vocabulary without approval.** This plan approves exactly: the folder names above, `test/sim/world/`, `docs/PRINCIPLES.md`, `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json`, `claudinite-run-cost`. Any other new label, word, field, file-name convention or term is filed as a question, never introduced.
5. **Breaking changes get hand-holding.** A change to what a member's mount, workflow or routine does — a path, a label, a field, a file a member reads — parks as `needs-human-action` naming the change; the folders `queue/`, `shared-code/`, `stubs/`, `worldRules/`, `workRules/`, `migrations/` sit outside every automerge policy in this plan.
6. **Subagents are fine inside a link**; a link stays one PR with one exit.

## Work paths

| Path | Scope (touches) | Contract (must not change) | Exit (readable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P — Principles** | `docs/`, the `test/sim/` guard, `§` pointers in code comments and pack prose, the README pointer | scenario test titles (the claim map binds to them) | `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` is the only file under `docs/`, the guard is green both ways |
| **S — Structure** | the whole pack tree, consumer packs' import lines, the barrier config, the pack README | the wire vocabulary, the seven frozen paths, every `shared-code/` export, `executor.md`/`instructions.md` locations | suite green, the barrier and line-match checks green on the new tree, this repo's own scheduler and executor green from the shim paths |
| **H — Harness** | `test/sim/` only; an engine fix a scenario proves necessary parks | scenario titles; every contract | `sim.mjs` holds no mechanism model; every scenario drives the real modules through the fake world |
| **R — Rewrite** | one `src/<stage>/` per link | everything above, `test/` untouched | the stage's line and module counts down, suite and sim green |
| **M — Measure** | `tasks/`, `src/world/` (the counter), the dashboard's readers and one panel | the session-usage file's keys during the stated window | the tasks usage file lands nightly and the dashboard reads it |
| **V — Verify** | nothing in the tree | — | runs read green; the retrospective answered against numbers recorded before and after R |

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup

None. Every read uses the Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## The plan

Each step is a queued link (`task:origin:ad-hoc`, `Blocked-by:` its predecessor). The chain advances on a link's exit reading true, never on its run having happened; every link's brief opens by reading its predecessor's artifact on `main` and converges as `action` naming the unmerged link when it is absent. No link's PR carries `Closes #<this issue>`.

- [ ] **P** — `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` from the current docs and the coverage map, the two-way claim guard, the design docs deleted, every `§` pointer re-pointed at a principle or dropped. *Policy: nothing (the principles are the design).*
- [ ] **S1** (#1478) — the re-shelve: `src/<role>/`, typed world ports with injectable shells, `pickOrder`/`evaluatePrecondition` extracted, the seven frozen paths as runnable shims carrying `@legacy-tolerance … retire:#S2`, `shared-code/` re-exporting `src/contract/`, consumer imports rewritten, tests mirroring `src/`, the barrier rules and line-match check, the README's layout table, `run.mjs`/`slots.mjs` and the slot-era `dispatch`/`resolve-dispatch`/`validate-dispatch` retired or placed per fielded history. *Policy: nothing (wide by nature).*
- [ ] **H1** (#1347) — the fake world in `test/sim/world/`, promoted from `executor-loop.test.mjs`'s fake repo; the loop test moved onto it with no behaviour change. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test`.*
- [ ] **H2** — every scenario ported onto the real code, the model deleted slice by slice, the "unsimulated world" table becoming each fake module's header plus limitation scenarios with their principles. A disagreement is decided by the principle; an engine fix parks. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/docs`.*
- [ ] **M1** — the tasks usage file: a `tasks-usage-fold` task, the run-cost record printed by each run and counted at the world ports, billed minutes from the jobs listing, the session fold dropping task keys after a stated window, the dashboard reading the new file. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/world; under:packs/claudinite-dashboard` (an engine `.gitattributes` seed parks).*
- [ ] **M2** — the dashboard's reliability and cost panel, per task and per member, window over window. *Policy: nothing (first render).*
- [ ] **R0** — the contract pins. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test`.*
- [ ] **R1** — rewrite `contract/` + `items/`. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/contract; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/items`.*
- [ ] **R2** — rewrite `schedule/` + `signals/`. *Policy: its folders.*
- [ ] **R3** — rewrite `execute/`. *Policy: its folder.*
- [ ] **R4** — rewrite `session/` + `deliver/`. *Policy: its folders.*
- [ ] **R5** — rewrite `recover/` + `adopt/` + the pack's own `tasks/`. *Policy: its folders.*
- [ ] **S2** — retire the `shared-code/` shims and the barrier's second allow path, 14 days after S1 merged (the window an active member needs to receive the engine that unblocks a held-back pack; a member stale longer takes the break). *Policy: nothing.*
- [ ] **V1** — after S1 merged, this repo's next scheduler run and executor run are green from the shim paths. No PR.
- [ ] **V2** — the retrospective, 7 days after the last of R5, M2, S2. No PR.

### The graph

```
P → S1 → H1 → H2 → R0 → R1 → R2 → R3 → R4 → R5 ─┐
     ├→ M1 → M2 ─────────────────────────────────┼→ V2
     ├→ S2 (Not-before: S1 + 14d) ───────────────┘
     └→ V1
```

M runs beside the main chain so the numbers exist before R starts.

### Human gates

`nothing` links: P, S1, M2, S2 — four. Expected parks: H2 (an engine fix beside the port), M1 (a seed outside its folders). **About six arrivals of the owner's attention across fifteen links.**

## Not in this chain

- #1346 (the `taskScheduler` config move) stays behind #1317; S1 leaves the config reader where it is.
- #1816 (the pack-boundary retrospective) stays under #1317; V2 is this plan's own.
- #1328 (the `updates/*` shims) is #1317's last code link.
- Simplifying the unit-test tree itself (re-homing tests onto stage entry points) — a later plan, once R shows which module paths the tests still need.

## The retrospective's brief (V2, written now)

Expected after the chain, against the numbers M1 records before R0:

| Measure | Now | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| non-test modules in the pack | 90 | ≤ 60 |
| non-test lines | ~11,000 | ≤ 7,000 |
| design-doc lines under `docs/` | 9,483 | ≤ 400 |
| scenarios | 82 | ≥ 100; the sim suite ≤ 5 s |
| principles without a scenario | not measured | 0 (the guard) |
| API calls per scheduler tick on a quiet day | not measured | recorded before R, not higher after |
| billed minutes per member-day | not measured | recorded before R, not higher after |
| barrier firings on a stage edge | none possible | 0 after S1 |
| `shared-code/` importers | 40 files | 0 after S2 |

Signals — misuse: a barrier finding on a stage edge, or a waiver added to let one through. Overuse: a shim still imported after S2. Underuse: a scenario cited by no principle; a panel nobody opened (page hits are not recorded — say so). The decision to re-examine: whether the roles are the right cut, read off which folders each of R1–R5's diffs actually touched and which parks they took.

## Corrections made while filing (2026-09-07, before any implementation)

- **S2 is dropped.** `shared-code/` stays the published surface, unrenamed: it publishes delivery and GitHub helpers too, which `contract/` would misname, and keeping the address needs no tolerance and nothing to retire. Its modules re-export from the new internal homes (S1's brief). The `nothing` gates are therefore three: P, S1, M2. The `shared-code/` importers row in the retrospective's table reads *unchanged by design* instead of *0 after S2*.
- **M1 keeps the session fold's task keys.** Their writers are marked `@deprecated` naming the tasks file as successor; removal is a later plan rather than a windowed tolerance inside this one.
- **V1 re-arms itself** (`Not-before:` to now + `Retry-every:`, status cleared) while the next tick has not come, rather than parking on a person.
- **The two reused issues are not sub-issues** of this one: the API needs their database id, which the session's tools do not return. They are linked here instead.

+// THE CLOCK PORT. Reading "now" is an edge to the world exactly like a REST call
+// is: it makes a run's answer depend on something outside its inputs. Every
+// module under `src/` that needs the current instant asks here, so a simulator
+// can drive a whole run at a chosen instant by replacing this one implementation
+// and nothing else changes hands.
+//
+// Parsing a timestamp is NOT a clock read — `new Date(iso)` over a string a
+// caller supplied is arithmetic, stays where it is used, and is deliberately
+// outside what this port covers.
+
+// The current instant, as a Date. The one place `new Date()` is called with no
+// argument anywhere under `src/`.
+export const now = () => new Date();
+
+// The current instant in epoch milliseconds — for durations and unique suffixes,
+// where a Date object would only be unwrapped again.
+export const nowMs = () => Date.now();
+
+// The current instant as the ISO-8601 string the queue's records are written in.
+export const nowIso = () => new Date().toISOString();

+// THE GITHUB ACTIONS PORT — the runner's environment, named. Everything the
+// scheduler and the executor learn from the job they are running inside comes
+// through here: which repository and branch, which run, which of our own
+// variables the workflow passed down, where the checkout is, and the one channel
+// a step has for handing a value to the next one.
+//
+// Why it is a port rather than `process.env` at the call site: the names are the
+// platform's, not ours, and a run driven by a simulator has no runner at all. One
+// module knowing `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_RUN_ID` and `GITHUB_OUTPUT` is what
+// lets every other module say what it needs instead of where it comes from.
+
+import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+
+// The raw environment, for the modules that take an `env` object and read a name
+// the caller chose (a task's declared secrets, an endpoint's token). They ask for
+// the bag rather than reaching for the global, so a fake environment is one
+// argument away everywhere the bag is threaded.
+export const actionsEnv = () => process.env;
+
+// The checkout the job is running in. The scheduler, the executor and the
+// converge all run Action-side inside the repository, so the working directory is
+// the tree they read tasks and config from.
+export const repoRoot = () => process.cwd();
+
+// The scheduler workflow's file name — the vendored shim's, identical in every
+// member (the workflow is core, not pack content). Named here rather than
+// restated: the usage fold finds a repo's scheduler runs by it, to read their
+// logs for the task-invocation records.
+export const SCHEDULER_WORKFLOW_FILE = 'claudinite-scheduler.yml';
+
+// The executor workflow's file name, same contract: identical in every member,
+// and the target of every `workflow_dispatch` in the queue's chain (PRINCIPLES.md)
+// — the close-time drain, a run's own re-dispatch, and the failure continuation.
+export const EXECUTOR_WORKFLOW_FILE = 'claudinite-executor.yml';
+
+// The repo slug (owner/name) and default branch the workflow runs against.
+// `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is always set in a workflow; `GITHUB_REF_NAME` is the
+// branch for a scheduled/dispatch run on the default branch.
+export function actionRepoContext(env = process.env) {
+  return {
+    repo: env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY || null,
+    defaultBranch: env.GITHUB_REF_NAME || 'main',
+  };
+}
+
+// The URL of the run doing the reporting, or null outside Actions.
+export const runUrl = (env = process.env) => (env.GITHUB_RUN_ID
+  ? `${env.GITHUB_SERVER_URL ?? 'https://github.com'}/${env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${env.GITHUB_RUN_ID}`
+  : null);
+
+// This run's URL for an arbitrary repo slug — the executor stamps its own run on
+// items in the repo it is draining, which is the repo it runs in, but it holds
+// the slug already and should not have to trust the environment for both halves.
+export const runUrlFor = (repo, env = process.env) => (env.GITHUB_RUN_ID
+  ? `${env.GITHUB_SERVER_URL ?? 'https://github.com'}/${repo}/actions/runs/${env.GITHUB_RUN_ID}`
+  : null);
+
+// Who is claiming an item. A run id makes the claim traceable back to the job
+// that made it; `local` is the hand-run case, which arbitration treats as any
+// other actor.
+export const executorId = (env = process.env) => env.CLAUDINITE_EXECUTOR_ID
+  || `actions-${env.GITHUB_RUN_ID ?? 'local'}`;
+
+// A step output, for the next step's `if:`. Outside Actions there is no output
+// file and nothing to write — a hand-run scheduler run simply has no consumer.
+export function setStepOutput(name, value, env = process.env) {
+  const out = env.GITHUB_OUTPUT;
+  if (!out) return false;
+  appendFileSync(out, `${name}=${value}\n`);
+  return true;
+}

+// The two shapes are genuinely different and stay separate: code-work is long,

+// "run a command" helper would have to serve both and would serve neither.

+import { spawn, execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
+
+// Start a command and stream its output. Returns the child, so the caller owns the
+// timeout, the kill and whatever it does with the streams — the executor's leash
+// is policy and does not belong down here.
+export const startProcess = (command, args, options) => spawn(command, args, options);
+
+// Run git and read its stdout. `maxBuffer` is generous on purpose: a generated
+// file can be large, and a `git show` of one easily tops spawn's default 1 MiB —
+// which fails as a truncated read, not as an error.
+//

+// an `input` set silently feeds the child NOTHING, and `hash-object --stdin` then
+// cheerfully writes the empty blob — a wrong answer, not an error.
+export const runGit = (args, opts = {}) => execFileSync('git', args, {
+  encoding: 'utf8',

1	// THE GITHUB PORT. Every REST path this pack calls is spelled in this module and
2	// nowhere else: a caller names the OPERATION it wants — read this issue, swap this
3	// label, merge this pull request — and never the URL that performs it. That is
4	// what makes the outward edge countable and replaceable; a module that spelled its
5	// own path would be a second GitHub client nothing knows about.
6	//
7	// The transport is `gh(path) -> { status, json }`, made by `makeGh` and passed to
8	// every operation as its first argument. It stays an injected function rather than
9	// a bound client because the whole pack tests against a fake `gh`, and because the
10	// fleet planner supplies its own reader over a different token.
11	//
12	// A non-2xx returns `{ status, json: null }` rather than throwing, so a 404 (no
13	// release yet, missing file) is data, not an error. Callers that must not mistake
14	// a refusal for an answer read the STATUS — a 403 from a repo whose Actions cannot
15	// write puts a plausible object where the result should be.
16	//
17	// LABEL WRITES ARE GRANULAR, ALWAYS (docs/PRINCIPLES.md): add and remove NAMED
18	// labels (POST/DELETE), never write the label SET (PUT). A set-write replaces from
19	// a stale snapshot and clobbers concurrent transitions — a bug class GitHub's own
20	// CLI shipped (cli/cli#4861) — and with a scheduler run and several executors all
21	// moving labels at once, that is a correctness rule rather than a style preference.

23	const API = process.env.GITHUB_API_URL || 'https://api.github.com';

25	// The Action-side reader/writer. `packs/claudinite-tasks/` is the one place that
26	// legitimately uses the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` — everything session-side stays
27	// MCP-only (docs/PRINCIPLES.md).

29	// `path` is an API path beginning with `/` (e.g. `/repos/owner/name/commits`); the
30	// base URL and auth are applied here.
31	export function makeGh({ token = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN, api = API, fetchImpl = fetch } = {}) {
32	  // `gh(path)` reads; `gh(path, { method, body })` writes (body JSON-encoded).
33	  return async function gh(path, { method = 'GET', body } = {}) {
34	    const res = await fetchImpl(`${api}${path}`, {
35	      method,
36	      headers: {
37	        accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
38	        'x-github-api-version': '2022-11-28',
39	        ...(token ? { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}),
40	        'user-agent': 'claudinite-scheduler',
41	        ...(body ? { 'content-type': 'application/json' } : {}),
42	      },
43	      ...(body ? { body: JSON.stringify(body) } : {}),
44	    });
45	    let json = null;
46	    try { json = await res.json(); } catch { json = null; }
47	    return { status: res.status, json };

import json, pathlib, collections

P = 'packs/claudinite-tasks/src/'

  edge(WORLD, [ENGINE, CONTRACT, ITEMS],

  edge(P+'signals', [ENGINE, CONTRACT, ITEMS, WORLD],
       "collection reads the world through the ports and describes it in the contract's terms; it decides nothing, so it names no stage"),
  edge(P+'schedule', [ENGINE, CONTRACT, ITEMS, WORLD, SIGNALS],
       "the schedule asks whether a task's window has opened and files the item — what happens to that item afterwards is another stage's, reached through the queue and never through an import"),
  edge(P+'execute', [ENGINE, CONTRACT, ITEMS, WORLD, SIGNALS, DELIVER],
       "the executor runs an item and hands its output to the delivery lane; it never reaches back into scheduling or into what a session does with the item it was handed"),
  edge(P+'session', [ENGINE, CONTRACT, ITEMS, WORLD, SIGNALS, DELIVER],
       "a session converges the item it was handed and lands its output; it is downstream of the executor and imports nothing from it"),
  edge(P+'deliver', [ENGINE, CONTRACT, ITEMS, WORLD, SIGNALS],
       "the landing lane is the bottom stage — it turns an output into a pull request and knows nothing about who produced it"),
  edge(P+'recover', [ENGINE, CONTRACT, ITEMS, WORLD, SIGNALS],

  edge(P+'adopt', [ENGINE, CONTRACT, ITEMS, WORLD, SIGNALS],
       "adoption writes a member's workflows from the declarations and touches no running stage"),
  {"from": 'packs/claudinite-tasks/src',

   "scope": "imports",
   "reason": "`queue/` is frozen workflow ABI and `shared-code/` is the published surface: both re-export the mechanism, so a module under src/ importing one would close a cycle through a path that exists only for outside callers"},
]

cd /home/user/Claudinite && git add -A && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
claudinite-tasks: roles as folders — src/<role>/, world ports, queue/ frozen as ABI

The pack was the old flat engine/scheduler/ copied in whole: ~90 modules with
queue/ holding both the workflow ABI and most of the mechanism. Nothing said
which part owned what.

Every module now sits in the role it plays — src/contract/, src/items/,
src/world/, src/signals/ and the stages src/schedule/, src/execute/,
src/session/, src/deliver/, src/recover/, src/adopt/ — and the graph between
them is one-directional and enforced by declared barrier rules. src/world/ is
the only place that reaches outside: every REST path the pack calls is a named
operation there, and the Actions environment, subprocesses and the clock are
ports beside it, with a declared line-match check keeping fetch(, process.env,
child_process and the argless clock reads out of everything else under src/.

pickOrder moves to src/items/ (both the schedule and the executor ask it) and
evaluatePrecondition to src/contract/, which leaves the DAG with no backward
edge. queue/ keeps the six workflow entry points as runnable shims plus
instructions.md and tasks/implement-request/ — the paths a member's workflows
and routines name literally, which a converge can never push. shared-code/
stays the published surface, re-exporting from the new internal homes, so no
consumer's non-test import changes.

run.mjs and slots.mjs are retired: the trunk's pack history names no fielded
importer of either, and the shim drift guard they carried now watches the
frozen queue entry points instead.

Refs #1869 #1478

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016Ep9aot1Q9Z48UTjxaGGAY
EOF

1:# claudinite-tasks — scheduled work
12:## Layout
31:## `shared-code/` — the one sanctioned cross-pack import
53:## Adoption
61:## Checks
=== layout section ===
## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `queue/` | the work item and its vocabulary, the scheduler run, the executor and its continuation, the drain, leases, readiness, the janitor's rules, workflow-failure escalation |
| `queue/tasks/` | the built-in tasks (`implement-request`) |
| `signals/` | the signal collectors a precondition is handed |
| `stubs/` | the two workflow files an adopting repo receives |
| `shared-code/` | the published import surface — see below |
| `tasks/` | this pack's own tasks: `task-janitor` (the queue's sweeps), `usage-fold` (it folds this mechanism's run records and outcome labels) and `verify-production` (coded production validations — URL probes judged as code-work) |
| `worldRules/` | the task-declaration checks |
| `workRules/` | the armed-auto-merge gate (`automerge-policy-scope`) |
| `precondition-policy.mjs` | the precondition engine: the `preconditions` expression grammar (a conjunction, `\|\|` inside a term, inline `:` arguments, the run-history terms `due:`/`last-run-over:`/`last-run-not-failed` that say how often; never whether the scheduler asks the task, which its `trigger` says), the built-in term vocabulary and its three-valued semantics, the derived signal union, and the loud fail direction |
| `task-terms.mjs`, `tasks/<name>/preconditions.mjs` | a task's OWN precondition terms — the extension point beside the declaration that names them |
| `task-trailer.mjs` | the `Claudinite-Task:` commit trailer the delivery lanes stamp and the movement signals classify by — how a task's own output is told from the project moving |
| `merge-policy.mjs` | the auto-merge policy engine: what a task's `automerge`, an item's `Merge:` field and the arming trailer mean, the built-in diff classes, the inline `under:<dir>` folder scope, the `&&` intersection, and the `merge-rules.json` vocabulary a pack extends them with |
| `test/` | the unit suite, and `test/sim/` — the simulator and its scenario suite, the mechanism's executable spec |
| `executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`, `deliver-pr.md` | operational documents a member's routines and workers read out of their own mount at runtime |

## `shared-code/` — the one sanctioned cross-pack import

Another pack's code may import `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*`, and nothing else of this
pack. The `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory; no other pack gains an
equivalent surface by existing.

| Module | What it publishes | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| `work-items.mjs` | the title grammar that is a work item's identity, the outcome/status decode over its labels, lease state, the dispatch vocabulary, and which items are a task's standing ones | claudinite-dashboard, claudinite-fleet-sheepdog |
| `anchors.mjs` | period length, and the instant a task's window last opened at or opens next | claudinite-dashboard |
| `delivery.mjs` | `landPr`, `deliverGenerated` — how a task's output becomes a landed PR or a regenerated file | any pack whose tasks deliver |
| `github.mjs` | the GitHub client and REST helpers, and the tracker issue a worker records on | any pack whose tasks reach GitHub |
| `signals.mjs` | the signal shapes a precondition is handed | packs asserting what their own tasks will see |
| `task-contract.mjs` | task-declaration validation, and the signal union either precondition form resolves to | every pack with tasks, in its own tests |
| `preconditions.mjs` | the precondition vocabulary, the expression grammar, and the one seam that turns a task plus its signals into a verdict — the call the executor makes at pick | every pack with tasks, in its own tests |
| `merge-policy.mjs` | the auto-merge policy verdict (`automerge`, the `Merge:` field, the arming trailer) and the `merge-rules.json` compiler | any pack declaring policies or merge rules, in its own tests |
| `usage-format.mjs` | the usage aggregate's codec | claudinite-fleet-sheepdog's fleet-wide aggregator |

A pack whose **non-task** code reads any of these declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`. A
pack's `tasks/` folder needs no declaration: a mount without this pack carries no `tasks/` at all,
since a task folder is inert without the queue that runs it.

## Adoption

The two workflow files and the routine endpoints cannot converge into place — `.github/workflows/`
is the one directory a member's nightly update may never write — so they are scaffolded once, at
adoption, by the `adopt-pack` skill. They are static from then on: the per-repo cron minute and
anchor hours are written once, secrets travel as one fixed line, and the `run:` lines name mount
pack paths behind which everything converges nightly.

## Checks

| Rule | Confidence | Dimension | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task-declaration-shape` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `task-code-work-env` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `automerge-policy-scope` | high | correctness | check: blocking |
| `legacy-task-fields` | low | complexity | check: advisory |
| `executor-workflow-secrets` | high | correctness | check: advisory |

The first two are relevance-first — inert until the repo carries a `tasks/<name>/task.json` of its own; the third is self-gating on the branch's own arming trailer.

- `task-declaration-shape` — a task declaration the scheduler reads is incomplete or illegal — no `preconditions` saying when it runs, an unknown condition, an illegal value — so the task never fires or fires wrong.
- `task-code-work-env` — a task reads a `CLAUDINITE_*` variable code-work never sets, so a parameter (a scope filter, a dry-run switch) silently never arrives and the run goes green in its most dangerous mode.
- `executor-workflow-secrets` — the executor workflow does not pass a secret the tasks of this repo's packs declare, so the queue picks the item up and only the run finds out the secret is not there. The list is the tasks' alone; an invocation endpoint's `tokenSecret` is config, stamped by the converge and reported by the invocation call itself. Advisory because the remedy is a human-merged PR to `.github/workflows/`, the one fix a member's own machinery cannot make.
- `automerge-policy-scope` — a branch that stamped the `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy` trailer (its run intends to land its own PR) carries a diff its declared policy does not cover, which is exactly the unreviewed change the policy exists to stop.

import pathlib, re

# one more named operation: reopening an issue.
p = pathlib.Path('src/world/github.mjs'); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace("export const postIssue = (gh, repo, body) =>",
"""export const reopenIssue = (gh, repo, number) =>
  gh(`/repos/${repo}/issues/${number}`, { method: 'PATCH', body: { state: 'open' } });

export const postIssue = (gh, repo, body) =>""")
p.write_text(s)

def imp(path, line):
    p = pathlib.Path(path); s = p.read_text()
    if line.strip() in s: return
    m = list(re.finditer(r"^import .*?;\n", s, re.M))
    p.write_text(s[:m[-1].end()] + line + s[m[-1].end():])

def rep(path, pairs, line=None):
    p = pathlib.Path(path); s = p.read_text()
    for a, b in pairs:
        assert a in s, (path, a[:80])
        s = s.replace(a, b)
    p.write_text(s)
    if line: imp(path, line)

 ('queue/executor-continuation.mjs',
  "// The continuation of a dead executor run: dispatches a fresh executor so the\n// queue drains rather than waiting for the next tick, and escalates when a chain\n// keeps dying.",
  'runExecutorContinuation', '../src/recover/continuation.mjs',
  [('../src/recover/continuation.mjs', ['runExecutorContinuation', 'continueOrEscalate',

input.body:
Link **S1** of #1869. Refs #1869 #1478 — this is one link of a longer chain, so it closes neither.

`packs/claudinite-tasks/` was the old flat `engine/scheduler/` copied in whole (#1326): 32 modules at the root, a `queue/` that was both workflow ABI and most of the logic, and REST paths spread over a dozen modules. Every module now sits in the role it plays, and the graph between the roles is enforced rather than described.

## What moved where

| Folder | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `src/contract/` | what a task declares and what it means — `task-contract`, `task-declaration{,-text}`, `task-defaults`, `task-terms`, `task-trailer`, `model-map`, `precondition-policy`, `calendar`, `merge-policy`, `built-in-tasks`, `discover`, `dormancy`, and the new `precondition.mjs` (the seam extracted from the executor) |
| `src/items/` | the work item as data — `work-item`, `leases`, `anchors`, `apply-status`, `read`, `run-record`, `tracker`, `usage-format`, `pr-fields`, and `pick-order` (also extracted from the executor) |
| `src/world/` | the only outward edges — `github.mjs` (the REST client and **every** call site's operation, named), `actions.mjs`, `sessions.mjs`, `git.mjs`, `processes.mjs`, `clock.mjs` |
| `src/signals/` | `index`, `context`, `fleet`, `for-task` (was `queue/signals.mjs`) |
| `src/schedule/` | `run` (was `queue/scheduler-run`), `readiness`, `create-work-item`, `drain-dispatch` |
| `src/execute/` | `loop` (was `queue/executor`), `heartbeat`, `suspend`, `target`, `code-work`, `code-work-run`, `prework-run`, the three env bags |
| `src/session/` | `converge-item`, `verify-outcome`, `record-exec`, `resolve-dispatch`, `validate-dispatch`, `dispatch` |
| `src/deliver/` | `land-pr`, `deliver-generated`, `deliver-pr.md` |
| `src/recover/` | `janitor-rules`, `workflow-failure`, `continuation` |
| `src/adopt/` | `converge-workflows`, `hash-minute` |
| `queue/` | the six frozen entry points as runnable shims, `instructions.md`, `tasks/implement-request/` — nothing else |
| `test/` | mirrors `src/`; `test/sim/` moved only its import paths |

`packs/claudinite-tasks/*.mjs` is now `pack.mjs` alone.

## Enforcement, landed with the tree

Two declared checks in `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/declared-checks.json`, both silent on the moved tree:

- **`tasks-stage-barriers`** — `forbidReferences` beside the existing `pack-independence` edge. `contract/` and `items/` name no stage and no world; `world/` imports at most `contract` and `items`; each stage imports only `contract`, `items`, `world`, `signals` and the stages below it (`execute` → `deliver`, `session` → `deliver`); nothing under `src/` imports `queue/` or `shared-code/`. Every rule's scope is non-empty against the real tree.
- **`tasks-world-edges-live-in-world`** — a line match keeping `fetch(`, `process.env`, `node:child_process`, argless `new Date()` and `Date.now(` under `src/` inside `src/world/` only.

## Deviations from the brief, and why

- **`pick-order.mjs` sits in `src/items/`, not `src/schedule/`.** Both stages ask it — the executor to choose what to claim, the scheduler run for `pickableCount`'s drain gate — and `items/` is the only role both may import. Putting it in `schedule/` would have created the execute → schedule edge the extraction exists to remove.
- **`continuation.mjs` sits in `src/recover/`, not `src/execute/`.** It escalates on `workflow-failure`'s surface, so placing it in `execute/` would have created an execute → recover edge. It is recovery by what it does.
- **`new Date()` is read as the argless clock read.** #1869's *End state* writes `new Date()`; the S1 text writes `new Date(`. Forbidding the latter would have moved `calendar.mjs` and every ISO-string parse into `world/`, which is arithmetic rather than an outward edge. The check forbids the clock read and leaves parsing where it is used; the module header says so.
- **The GitHub port is a module of named operations over the injected `gh`, not yet a bound port object.** Every REST path the pack calls is spelled in `src/world/github.mjs` and nowhere else, which is what makes the edge countable. Converting the *seam* from `gh(path)` to a port object means rewriting every test's fake, which is H1's job (`test/sim/world/`) and would have changed tests here, against this link's own shape.
- **`evaluatePrecondition`'s window arithmetic moved with it.** `defaultWindowMs` / `windowDaysOf` / `DAY_MS` are declaration-derived, so they live in `src/contract/precondition.mjs`; `src/signals/for-task.mjs` republishes them under the names its callers and tests already use.
- **`shared-code/github.mjs` also publishes `src/world/actions.mjs`.** `SCHEDULER_WORKFLOW_FILE`, `EXECUTOR_WORKFLOW_FILE` and `actionRepoContext` moved out of the REST client into the Actions port; the dashboard reads two of them through `shared-code`, so the published surface is unchanged from outside.
- **`isQueueItem` moved from `src/items/read.mjs` to `src/items/work-item.mjs`.** The dashboard loads it in a browser, and `read.mjs` now imports the GitHub port; the decoder is vocabulary, so it lives with the vocabulary and `read.mjs` republishes it.

## Slot-era survivors

`git log main -- packs/` names no fielded importer of `run.mjs` or `slots.mjs`, so both are deleted. That retires the `parseOverrides` drift guard against `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/param-bag.mjs` with them — `parseOverrides` had no non-test caller and no second copy is left to drift. The shim test's remaining row now watches the frozen `queue/` entry points instead, which is the live version of the same claim. `dispatch.mjs`, `resolve-dispatch.mjs` and `validate-dispatch.mjs` **are** fielded — `executor.md`'s routine runs `resolve-dispatch.mjs`, `shared-code/work-items.mjs` publishes `dispatch.mjs` and the task-janitor's worker imports it — so they moved to `src/session/` rather than retiring.

## Frozen surfaces

The six `queue/*.mjs` are runnable entry points: they import the real module, run its named entry when invoked directly, and **name** what the old path published rather than leaving it to `export *` — which also carries `pickOrder` and `evaluatePrecondition`, the two names that left the executor. `queue/instructions.md` and `executor.md` stay put and address the new homes from a base they derive from their own location (`<pack>` = `<here>/..`). `queue/tasks/implement-request/` did not move: `pathTo()` resolves the task by that literal path, which is written into every adopted issue's machine block.

`shared-code/` stays the published surface, unrenamed, re-exporting from the new internal homes — **no consumer's non-test import changes**. The `consumer-safe-change` rule is discharged by the re-export shims, which is the third answer its own fix text names; no migration record or rehearsal fixture is needed because nothing is removed.

## Exit, read on this branch

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **3393 pass, 1 fail**. The one failure is `every engine module a fielded pack version imports still resolves`, which asserts `origin/main~50` exists before trusting its history walk; this checkout is shallow at exactly 50 commits, so it fails identically on `main` (verified). CI checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — silent.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — silent.
- `ls packs/claudinite-tasks/*.mjs` lists `pack.mjs` alone; the six `queue/*.mjs` are shims.
- `test(` calls across the touched test files: 1157 before, 1157 after.

V1 (#1873) reads this repo's own scheduler and executor runs green from the shim paths once this merges.
